attacks.claim: The gsutil command is built as an f-string and run with shell=True. Partner-chosen filenames (src.stem) flow into the shell command, so a crafted SFTP filename containing shell metacharacters executes arbitrary commands on workers that hold GCS write credentials for the whole raw bucket. Filenames with spaces also break the command.

partition_date() switched from UTC to local time. Workers run with TZ=America/Los_Angeles, and the job runs at 01:30 UTC, so every nightly run writes into the previous day's dt partition (it overwrites same-named chunks there) and the UTC-date partition dashboards read never gets its marker.
attacks.evidence: return datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d") (previously datetime.now(timezone.utc)); artifact context: "Downstream dashboards read a dt=YYYY-MM-DD partition (UTC date)" and "scheduled at 01:30 UTC" with "TZ=America/Los_Angeles"

attacks.claim: The _SUCCESS marker is written unconditionally after per-file failures are caught and counted. Dashboards treat the marker as proof the partition is complete, so they will read partial data as final.
attacks.evidence: except Exception: log.exception(...); failed += 1 ... write_success_marker(BUCKET, f"raw/{partner}/dt={dt}/")

attacks.claim: ingest_partner never raises or returns a failure signal when failed > 0, so the Airflow task reports success and no alert fires. Failures appear only in a log line.
attacks.evidence: log.info("partner=%s dt=%s ok=%d failed=%d", partner, dt, ok, failed) with no raise or non-zero exit after the loop

attacks.claim: A failed file leaves its already-uploaded chunks in the raw partition, and reruns have no cleanup. Chunk count can change between runs, so stale chunks from an earlier attempt persist alongside new ones in the same dt partition.
attacks.evidence: chunk.unlink() only runs after a successful upload; ABSENT: deletion of previously uploaded chunks for a failed src or of stale objects under raw/{partner}/dt={dt}/{src_name}/ before rerun

attacks.claim: Local chunk files are not cleaned up when an exception is raised mid-file, because there is no try/finally. Large failing files (the 3.1 GB case) can accumulate gzip chunks in work_dir and fill the worker disk.
attacks.evidence: for chunk in _write_chunks(src, work_dir): _upload(...); chunk.unlink() inside try, with no cleanup in except

attacks.claim: The claim that normalisation is unchanged does not hold for its input. pandas read_csv(dtype=str) produced NaN for empty cells, while csv.DictReader produces '' with no dtype handling. The file is also opened with no explicit encoding, so behaviour depends on locale, and a UTF-8 BOM would corrupt the first column name.
attacks.evidence: with src.open(newline="") as fh: reader = csv.DictReader(fh) ... "Schema normalisation is unchanged (same `normalise_row`)."

attacks.claim: A file with zero data rows (empty or header-only) produces no chunks, but the loop still counts it as ok. Partner data silently goes missing and the partition is marked complete.
attacks.evidence: for chunk in _write_chunks(src, work_dir): ... ok += 1 (no check that any chunk was produced)

attacks.claim: The raw object layout changed from one object per source file (raw/{partner}/dt=/{stem}.csv.gz) to a directory of multiple chunk objects. Existing downstream readers that expect the old path will miss data or break, and the PR does not address this.
attacks.evidence: dest = f"gs://{BUCKET}/raw/{partner}/dt={dt}/{src_name}/{local.name}" (previously blob f"raw/{partner}/dt={dt}/{src.stem}.csv.gz"); ABSENT: reader or migration notes

attacks.claim: subprocess.run has no timeout, so a hung gsutil transfer blocks the worker and the Airflow task indefinitely.
attacks.evidence: subprocess.run(f"gsutil ...", shell=True, check=True) with no timeout argument

attacks.claim: The speed claim for gsutil parallel composite uploads over the client library is unmeasured. Composite uploads also create temporary component objects that need delete permissions and can leave orphans on failure.
attacks.evidence: "parallel composite uploads are much faster than the client library for multi-GB objects"; ABSENT: benchmark or orphan-cleanup handling

attacks.claim: Processing is single-threaded per row and sequential per file, and runtime for multi-GB files is not measured against the nightly window.
attacks.evidence: for src in sorted(drop_dir.glob("*.csv")): ... ABSENT: throughput or runtime measurement for the 3.1 GB feed

attacks.claim: The ingest_partner signature gains a required work_dir parameter. The diff does not update call sites, so existing callers will fail.
attacks.evidence: def ingest_partner(partner: str, drop_dir: Path, work_dir: Path) -> None: ABSENT: updated callers
